sources.name: Elena Soria Dominguez
sources.quote: Mr. Navarro — straight answer, from the record. **Construction has not begun. There is no construction on the Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II, and the tracker does not say there is.** What INIT-003 shows: - **Status:** passed; **ImplementationPhase: design-phase**. It has been in design-phase since C111. - **Payments:** none on INIT-003 this cycle. None. - **Work history:** my own work entries on INIT-003 are C113, C114, C115 — planning and review work, not construction. - **C117 note on the tracker, in plain language:** further design advancement is held; preliminary schematics and a documented Fruitvale public comment-and-response record are *not evidenced in the packet*. So, answering your two specific questions directly: 1. **Have preliminary schematics been delivered?** Not that the record shows. The tracker has mandated schematics delivery since C114 and repeated the requirement at C115 and C117. The C117 entry says they are not evidenced in the packet. Until they are in the packet, I will not tell you they are delivered. 2. **Does a Fruitvale comment-and-response record exist?** No. That record does not yet exist. Every comment that came in — in the language it came in — has to be answered before design advancement moves. That is the gate, and it is still closed. What the record *does* show is real but is not construction: merchant covenants executed, Mayer & Associates under contract with community oversight provisions, the visioning phase complete since C86. None of that is a shovel in the ground, and the Tribune's print saying otherwise is wrong. I'd ask for a correction. On the numbers, since they'll be in the same story: Fruitvale is at 8,007 riders this cycle, down from 9,343, on-time 0.85 against 0.83. The citywide pattern is event and game-day driven — crowded platforms, congestion 0.14 — and my East Oakland stations, Fruitvale and Coliseum, are both holding up. I'm not going to dress a ridership drop as progress on a drawing, and I'm not going to let a headline call this station under construction when it isn't. Next scheduled action is Cycle 118: deliver the preliminary schematics and publish the documented Fruitvale public comment-and-response record. When that's real, you'll have it from me first. — Elena Soria Dominguez, Transit Hub Planning Lead

assert: manifest.approvedFacts are canon — never contradict them
attribute: a named ledger citizen speaks only in manifest.approvedQuotes or their own page line; everyone else speaks in your words
limits.rule: The Packet is what you know, not the fence around what you may write. The approved facts and the ledger are canon: never contradict them, and never import real-world Oakland (its people, businesses, landmarks, troubles). Everything else — the scene, the street, the weather in the room, unnamed people and what they say, new in-world places and businesses, what the city is talking about — is yours to invent; that colour is the job, and it never rewrites a canon fact. A named ledger citizen speaks only in their approved quote or their own page line.

approvedQuotes.text: The Fruitvale community review is set for the first Thursday of next month at the Fruitvale Senior Center, 6 p.m., with the design team in the room — and yes, the held design covers the site work, because we're not letting construction outrun the community's say.

Mr. Navarro — straight answer, from the record. **Construction has not begun. There is no construction on the Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II, and the tracker does not say there is.** What INIT-003 shows: - **Status:** passed; **ImplementationPhase: design-phase**. It has been in design-phase since C111. - **Payments:** none on INIT-003 this cycle. None. - **Work history:** my own work entries on INIT-003 are C113, C114, C115 — planning and review work, not construction. - **C117 note on the tracker, in plain language:** further design advancement is held; preliminary schematics and a documented Fruitvale public comment-and-response record are *not evidenced in the packet*. So, answering your two specific questions directly: 1. **Have preliminary schematics been delivered?** Not that the record shows. The tracker has mandated schematics delivery since C114 and repeated the requirement at C115 and C117. The C117 entry says they are not evidenced in the packet. Until they are in the packet, I will not tell you they are delivered. 2. **Does a Fruitvale comment-and-response record exist?** No. That record does not yet exist. Every comment that came in — in the language it came in — has to be answered before design advancement moves. That is the gate, and it is still closed. What the record *does* show is real but is not construction: merchant covenants executed, Mayer & Associates under contract with community oversight provisions, the visioning phase complete since C86. None of that is a shovel in the ground, and the Tribune's print saying otherwise is wrong. I'd ask for a correction. On the numbers, since they'll be in the same story: Fruitvale is at 8,007 riders this cycle, down from 9,343, on-time 0.85 against 0.83. The citywide pattern is event and game-day driven — crowded platforms, congestion 0.14 — and my East Oakland stations, Fruitvale and Coliseum, are both holding up. I'm not going to dress a ridership drop as progress on a drawing, and I'm not going to let a headline call this station under construction when it isn't. Next scheduled action is Cycle 118: deliver the preliminary schematics and publish the documented Fruitvale public comment-and-response record. When that's real, you'll have it from me first. — Elena Soria Dominguez, Transit Hub Planning Lead
